| [CLAIM-1046](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1046.md) v2 | Probe partitions are not the decomposition lattice | A15 §2 says "the lattice of all partitions of Ω is generally much larger than the set of partitions realizable by our affordable probes", and that the probe lattice "is a structure of which distinctions our methods support", not of selves. For fixed configurations Ω and fixed response laws, let π(Q) be the partition of Ω into classes no probe in Q separates. Then π(Q1 ∪ Q2) is the meet (common refinement) of π(Q1) and π(Q2), while π(Q1 ∩ Q2) is at least as coarse as their join and can be strictly coarser. So π is order-reversing and meet-preserving, its image is a meet-closed part of the partition lattice and need not be a sublattice, and with m probes it has at most 2^m members, against Bell(\|Ω\|) partitions (32 against 115,975 for m = 5 and \|Ω\| = 10). Checked with python3 -I on 3,000 random probe systems (no union failed; the intersection was strictly coarser than the join in 100) and on an explicit case.
